sentences.text: This extinct flightless rail lived exclusively on the North Island of New Zealand.
It possessed the smallest wings relative to its body size among all known rail species.
Its legs, specifically the tarsometatarsus, were disproportionately large compared to the rest of its frame.
A bill measuring about 7 cm was very long for such a small creature.
The holotype specimen was discovered in Karamu Cave, situated 21 km from Hamilton.
The genus Capellirallus was formally described by Falla in 1954.
The species became extinct during the 13th century.
Fossils indicate the animal inhabited the western North Island, an area dominated by wet, closed-canopy rainforests.
Its long bill suggests the snipe-rail foraged by probing, similar to kiwi.
The snipe-rail belongs to the family Rallidae.
Its evolutionary relationships remain unclear, though bone structure suggests a possible link to the extinct Chatham rail.
It is debated when the snipe-rail went extinct, though researchers suggest its decline began in the 13th century due to the spread of the Polynesian rat.
